newsitem.title: CHINA: China seen short of polystyrene, polypropylene.
newsitem.headline: China seen short of polystyrene, polypropylene.

text.p: China likely will see demand rise this year for polystyrene and polypropylene, and imports were seen increasing, the China Chemical Industry News said on Monday The newspaper urged controls on polystyrene imports in 1997 after imports of more than 1.0 million tonnes in 1996 had pushed domestic stockpiles to about 300,000 tonnes.
Domestic demand for polystyrene would be about 1.2 million tonnes in 1997 and domestic output about 300,000 tonnes, up slightly from last year, it said without giving 1996 figures.
However, rising domestic demand for polypropylene this year, estimated at 2.2 million tonnes, would push up domestic prices.
The polypropylene shortage would be 950,000 tonnes although domestic output was expected to be 1.25 million tonnes, up 13.6 percent, or 150,000 tonnes, from last year, the newspaper said.
China's total demand for plastic raw materials was expected to be 11-12 million tonnes in 1997, up 29.4 percent from 1996.
China's shortage of plastic raw materials would be about 5.0 million tonnes while demostic supply this year was estimated at 7.0 million tonnes, the newspaper said.
